task.title: Update 5 skill files for markdown specs + MCP-driven state
task.description:
Five skill files need Phase 2 updates. Keep edits surgical — only where the file references XML task format, GOALS.md / DISCUSSION.md / BLUEPRINT.md as required workflow files, or in-file status / sign-off fields. Other content (chain-of-thought rules, worktree discipline, review checklists) stays.
**1. `skills/architect-workflow/SKILL.md`** — most invasive. - File Format Rules table: drop GOALS / DISCUSSION / BLUEPRINT rows; keep tasks/*.md row (replace XML with MD; format = "Markdown frontmatter + body"). - Workflow Steps numbered list: rewrite to "1. Create or resume MCP issue (issue_create or issue_resume) → 2. Discuss via discussion_append until aligned → 3. Author markdown task specs → 4. task_create_batch + task_set_spec_path → 5. Spawn SWE per task → 6. Validate per validate-swe-output → 7. PR Reviewer → 8. Close tasks via task_update_status(status='closed')." - Discussion Phase: replace the file-based DISCUSSION.md / ANSWER-BELOW marker workflow with the MCP discussion_append + conversational alignment workflow. Optionally generate a snapshot via issue_snapshot_md when the human wants a doc to review. - GOALS.md Change Detection: drop entirely (no GOALS.md file). Replace with a one-paragraph note: "If the human revises intent mid-workflow, append a new discussion_append(kind='intent') entry; re-evaluate the open task batch and split / cancel as needed via task_update_status."
**2. `skills/swe-spawn-workflow/SKILL.md`** — pin to markdown. - "Naming" line: change from `docs/trustmybot/tasks/<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>_<descriptive_name>.xml` to `docs/trustmybot/tasks/<branch_id_filename>.md` (the timestamp convention dies; branch_id is the index per blueprint change #F). - Replace the entire **Task File Template (XML)** code block with a markdown spec template: YAML frontmatter (per docs/trustmybot/SPEC-FORMAT.md) + body sections. Reference SPEC-FORMAT.md as the canonical contract; do not duplicate the full format here — keep this skill focused on spawn protocol. - Size limit: keep "200 lines maximum" but note "If this skill's template is exceeded, split into multiple specs with depends_on chains."
**3. `skills/swe-checklist/SKILL.md`** — VERIFIED format-agnostic by architect during task spec authoring. The file references section concepts in backticks (`<context>`, `<error-handling>`, `<edge-cases>`, `<verification>`, `<commit>`) but treats them as conceptual section names, not XML tag literals — they map 1:1 to markdown headings (`## Context`, `## Error Handling`, etc.) without semantic change. No status-attribute references. No GOALS/DISCUSSION/BLUEPRINT references.
Action: re-read the file once to re-confirm; if confirmation holds, NO EDITS. Document in the Results section: "swe-checklist was verified format-agnostic; section names in backticks read as concepts, not XML literals; no edits required." If anything new has appeared since the architect's read (a recent change added an XML literal), apply the surgical replacement and note it in Results.
**4. `skills/validate-swe-output.md`** (NOTE: this is a single-file skill at `skills/validate-swe-output.md`, not a directory) — update verification protocol: - Verify task row in MCP shows `status='completed'`, not the in-file `status` attribute. - Verify validation_attempts can be appended via validation_record. - Re-run the spec's `## Verification` block (markdown section, not XML element).
**5. `skills/review-protocol/SKILL.md`** — update review steps to cite MCP validation_record as the sign-off mechanism, not XML tag editing. Cite markdown spec section names where the old review protocol cited XML elements.
For each file: open it, read it fully (do not skim), and apply only the required substitutions. Many sections are agent-agnostic prose that stays.
Cite `docs/trustmybot/SPEC-FORMAT.md` exactly once per file (in the section that introduces task spec format).
